findings.title: Prophetic communication across the named line
findings.claim: The prophets named in the focus form a wider relay of divine communication across Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and their descendants.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus word ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ, whose messenger sense is independently met by the supplied wider texts that join the named figures to revelation, scripture, covenant, and one religion at 4:163, 33:7, 42:13, and 57:26. Their contact turns the catalogue into a connected line of transmitted divine news and mission rather than isolated names.
findings.reader_payoff: The breadth of the list becomes legible as continuity of a received message carried through prophetic generations.
findings.containment: The finding preserves the ordinary named-prophet catalogue; it does not make every descendant a prophet, supply target-side morphology, or claim a single theory of prophetic history.

epistemic.reason: The four cited connection rows are strong review nominations with exact target Arabic, while target-side morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied.

findings.title: Lineage preserved through carriage

findings.mechanism: The carrier is حَمَلْنَا in the focus phrase about those carried with Noah. The supplied wider texts at 17:3 repeat the exact descendants-of-those-carried-with-Noah relation, and 36:41 echoes descendants carried in the laden ship. The repeated contact makes the carriage event itself the bridge from Noah to later descendants.
findings.reader_payoff: The genealogy acquires movement and preservation: the line is not only named but shown continuing through what was carried onward.
findings.containment: The finding adds a supplied preservation image to the ordinary genealogy; it does not turn the phrase into a general theory of biological descent, establish an unprovided causal chain, or replace the plain reference to Noah's carried descendants.

findings.containment: The finding supports the ordinary divine favor and prophetic list; it does not claim that lineage guarantees guidance, collapse the focus into a reading of 1:7, or infer a target-side grammatical identity not supplied here.

findings.title: Recitation becomes an embodied response
findings.claim: Across the supplied wider texts, recited signs meet an embodied sequence of falling, prostration, and tears.
findings.mechanism: The focus's تُتْلَىٰ, خَرُّوا۟, and سُجَّدًا connect recitation to a physical fall and a prostrated body. The wider relations at 17:107, 17:109, and 32:15 independently repeat recited revelation or signs with falling, prostration, and weeping. Their contact changes the ending from a generic emotional reaction into a complete reception event in which hearing reaches bodily submission and tears.
findings.reader_payoff: The final movement can be felt as a chain from signs being recited, through impact and descent, to a body visibly lowered and overflowing.
findings.containment: The finding does not claim that recitation mechanically forces every hearer to respond, and it leaves the focus's plain report of the prophets' prostration and weeping intact.

findings.title: Reception remains a responsive choice
findings.claim: The wider field places the focus's humble bodily reception beside live forms of proud denial and refusal, making the response a distinguishable posture rather than an automatic effect of recitation.
findings.mechanism: The focus records recited signs followed by falling, prostration, and weeping. The supplied 19:73 relation sets recited clear signs against proud denial, and 45:8 sets hearing recited signs against persistent arrogance. These contrary responses return through the same recitation-and-response act and sharpen what the focus's descent and tears do.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's bodily lowering becomes legible as receptive action: the signs can be encountered, yet the hearer's posture still marks the direction taken.
findings.containment: The contrasting ayat are counter-evidence about the wider response field, not a claim that rejection occurs in the focus. Both the focus's humble response and the wider contrary responses remain live.

epistemic.reason: Both cited connections are strong review nominations with exact target Arabic and explicit contrast notes; target-side morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Tears remain a response without one imposed motive
findings.claim: The focus's tears remain a real embodied response while their inward affect stays open across the wider counter-images.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's final weeping state, paired with prostration. The supplied relations place that response against the absence of cosmic weeping at 44:29, set weeping beside laughter as an effect at 53:43, reverse it with laughter at 53:60, and contrast it with commanded weeping at 9:82. The contact preserves the tears as meaningful overflow while preventing one unprovided inward cause from being imposed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the full force of tears joined to prostration without reducing them to one named emotion or treating them as decorative intensity.
findings.containment: The finding does not establish tenderness, grief, warning, gratitude, or any other single cause; it keeps the focus's plain weeping and records the wider affective boundary supplied by the connections.

epistemic.reason: The four cited rows are medium connection nominations with exact target Arabic and contrast notes; they support an affective boundary but do not provide a single interior explanation.
